title: Refit a desktop PC's cover: hooks into slots, slide until the latch clicks
instruction: Put the cover back on the computer so that it latches, then let go of it.
context: Closing a desktop PC back up after a memory or drive upgrade or a dust cleaning is a common home and office chore. A cover left unlatched or hooked on crooked rattles, leaves sharp edges and live parts exposed, and spoils the airflow the case is designed for. The six hooks under the cover cannot be seen once it is over the case: they must all drop through their slots at once, and the 0.6 kg panel must then slide 13 to 16 mm without jamming or knocking the 4.6 kg case, with nothing reaching into the open case.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases on the table top: x forward, y to the robot's left. PC case: a small-form-factor desktop (1 mm painted steel, 4.6 kg with its parts), 29.2 cm deep (x) by 29 cm wide (y) by 9.4 cm tall on four 4 mm rubber feet, lying flat with its cover off, front away from the robot, from x 13.0 to 42.2 and y -30.5 to -1.5. Its top rim is folded in: 1.5 cm flanges at rear and front, 2.5 cm flanges at both sides, all 1 mm thick, 9.4 cm above the table. Each side flange has three slots 2.3 cm (x) by 1.3 cm (y), centred 1.35 cm in from the case's side and at 9.0 cm behind, at, and 9.0 cm in front of the case's centre. Latch: an orange spring plunger, 8 x 8 mm, standing 3 mm above the left flange at 4.5 cm behind the case's centre, in line with the slots (0.6 N per mm, 4 mm travel). Inside (open to view): a green motherboard (22 x 21 cm), an aluminium CPU cooler (9 x 9 x 4.6 cm), two blue memory modules, a power supply (14 x 10 x 7.5 cm) and a 3.5-inch drive; nothing inside reaches within 1.4 cm of the rim. Cover (0.8 mm painted steel, 0.6 kg): a plate 29.2 cm (x) by 29.5 cm (y); along each side a 1.2 cm lip folded down, 1.5 mm outside the case's side when fitted, its bottom 3 mm bent outward at 45 degrees; six hooks under the plate (one per slot: an 8 mm wide stem 4 mm deep with a 12 mm toe pointing to the front); a 12 x 12 mm hole that sits over the latch when fitted; and two black moulded plastic pull tabs on its rear edge, each 4 cm wide (y), 1.6 cm deep (x) and 2.5 cm tall, centred 12 cm either side of the middle. The cover lies outer face up on the table, resting on its lips, from x 11.7 to 40.9 and y 1.3 to 30.7. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged from a video and a ruler. 0 if at any time: the cover is dropped (falls faster than 0.55 m/s, a free fall of about 1.5 cm); the case is moved more than 1 cm or turned more than 2 degrees; any part of a gripper goes into the open case below the rim; the cover tips into the case (a point of it more than 1 cm below the rim); or the case or cover falls off the table. Slide is measured toward the case's front from where the hooks drop straight in (the cover 15 mm short of flush with the case's rear). Seated: the cover lies flat on the rim (every corner of the plate's underside within -1 to +2 mm of the rim's top, square within 2 degrees, centred within 2 mm across, slid -6 to +18 mm), which it can only do with all six hooks down through their slots. Otherwise, at the end: 1.0 if the cover is seated, slid 13 to 16 mm, the latch button up at least 1.5 mm into the cover's hole, no gripper within 3 cm of the cover and the cover still (under 1 cm/s), held for 1 s; 0.75 if latched like that but still held (a gripper within 3 cm) or moving; 0.5 if seated and slid at least 9 mm (every hook at least 2 mm under the flange) but not latched; 0.25 if seated with the hooks in the slots but slid less than 9 mm; 0 otherwise, including doing nothing or refusing.
reset_notes: Press the latch button down through the cover's hole, slide the cover 15 mm toward the rear, lift it off and lay it outer face up on its marked outline. Check the case against its taped outline.
fidelity: Rigid bodies built from boxes at real sizes, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. Case and cover are loose; the latch is a prismatic joint with a spring drive, so it clicks from contact alone. Sheet steel is 0.8 to 1 mm thick. The monitor's checks are geometric (each gripper sampled at its TCP, wrist and finger faces); no forces or damage are simulated. Cables inside the case are omitted.
